rules.unsafe_description: A Safe Walkway Violation is defined as movement or presence outside the boundaries of the green-marked Designated Safe Walkway.
rules.safe_description: Safe Walkway is defined as movement along the production floor that remains within the boundaries of the green-marked Designated Safe Walkway.
rules.callout_text: The Safe Walkway Violation is the highest-frequency unsafe behavior recorded at this facility. The frequency of this behavior reflects a tendency among personnel to treat minor deviations from the walkway as inconsequential. Any deviation from the green-marked boundaries places the individual in proximity to forklift and machinery hazards and will be treated as an unsafe behavior event requiring immediate response.
rules.source_quote: A Safe Walkway Violation is defined as movement or presence outside the boundaries of the green-marked Designated Safe Walkway.

rules.observable_indicator: Person interacting with equipment without green vest or without required safety equipment
rules.unsafe_description: An Unauthorized Intervention is defined as any of the following observable situations: - A person interacting with or adjusting production equipment while wearing a red-black vest or any vest other than the designated green authorization vest.
rules.safe_description: An Authorized Intervention is defined as an interaction with or working on production equipment performed by a person who is wearing the designated green safety vest and the required safety equipment for the task.
rules.callout_text: The green safety vest is the primary and most readily observable indicator of authorization status. Any person seen interacting with equipment who is not wearing the green vest must be assumed to be performing an Unauthorized Intervention. This classification applies regardless of the person's stated intent or role, since the vest system exists precisely to make authorization status unambiguous to observers and to the automated monitoring system.
rules.source_quote: An Unauthorized Intervention is defined as any of the following observable situations: - A person interacting with or adjusting production equipment while wearing a red-black vest or any vest other than the designated green authorization vest.

rules.observable_indicator: Panel cover in open position during production operations
rules.unsafe_description: Opened Panel Cover is defined as the condition in which the cover of an electrical panel connected to a production machine has been left in the open position.
rules.safe_description: Closed Panel Cover is defined as the condition in which the cover of an electrical panel connected to a production machine is fully closed.
rules.callout_text: Leaving a panel cover open - even when doing so feels like a minor or temporary oversight - is classified as an unsafe behavior under this Manual. The automated detection system monitors panel cover status continuously and will generate an alert whenever an open-cover condition is observed.
rules.source_quote: Opened Panel Cover is defined as the condition in which the cover of an electrical panel connected to a production machine has been left in the open position.

rules.observable_indicator: 3 or more blocks on forklift forks
rules.unsafe_description: Carrying Overload with Forklift is defined as operating a forklift while carrying three (3) or more standardized blocks in a single load.
rules.safe_description: Safe Carrying is defined as operating a forklift while carrying two (2) or fewer standardized blocks in a single load.
rules.callout_text: The block count threshold is unambiguous: two blocks or fewer is safe; three blocks or more is an overload. Any observed forklift load of three or more standardized blocks will be treated as a Carrying Overload with Forklift event and will trigger an immediate alert.
rules.source_quote: Carrying Overload with Forklift is defined as operating a forklift while carrying three (3) or more standardized blocks in a single load.
